# claude.md - Register Errands - Dynamic (tree 518765124) ## Purpose ETG (eTraveli Group) agent workflow, embedded in Zendesk. For a cancellation contact, the agent looks up the Edvin order, selects PNRs/passengers/channel/type, picks a customer action per PNR, and the tree auto-creates the Zendesk child/silent/grandchild tickets, registers the errand in Edvin, and posts an internal note. ## Architecture (flow) - REWRITTEN FOR v46, 2026-09-02 Everything below is verified against this export's actual node ids. The three DRIFT/CORRECTION notes that used to live here are gone: they described node numbers from v26/v37/v42 that have not existed for several versions, and keeping them meant every reader had to work out which half of the section to believe. Anything earlier than v45 in the Changelog is history, not a map. Root = 10 (Clear session and start fresh order). INTAKE 10 -> 77 Verify Order Reference -> 4 Edvin Find Order -> 13 status 13 -> 61 Insert Linked PNRs -> 6 Select PNRs -> 24 Set order context & channel 24 -> 54 PNR selection made? -> [55 re-pick] | 75 Is VI selection? -> [76 VI subtree] | 7 7 Set Selected PNRs -> 8 Select Passengers -> 9 Format Passengers -> 56 selection made? 56 -> [57 re-pick] | 42 GET Edvin Errands -> 26 status -> 46 Format Types -> 1 Select Channel & Type -> 2 Build actions_array + push PNR -> 11 More PNRs? -> loop to 7, else 12 12 Create PNR Action Table -> 25 Display table -> 58 Check selections -> 59 all picked? 59 -> [60 re-pick] | 27 GROUPING 27 Stitch & Group -> builds transforms.work_queue + transforms.final_pnrs -> 3 TICKET LOOP (ONE loop, child + silent + grand child - v45) 3 Any tickets to create? -> [none: 21] | 32 32 Loop Tickets (cursor) -> 84 Validate Ticket Data -> 33 Create Ticket (CO #20) -> 17 status 17 -> 62 Updating Tickets -> 64 Set Side Conversation Id -> 63 Get Ticket Details (CO #158) 39 status -> 65 Resolve Ticket Id -> 66 Update Ticket (CO #207) -> 41 status -> 34 34 Is More Tickets? -> loop to 32, else 21 ERRAND LOOP 21 Format Internal Note -> 22 Add Internal Note (CO #57) -> 15 status 15 -> 44 Loop Errands to Register (cursor) -> 78 Validate Errand Details -> 43 Register Errand (CO #160) -> 30 status 30 -> 83 Is More PNRs? -> loop to 44, else 23 CLOSE 23 Closing Call 23 -> [47 Additional/Different Request -> 29 Clear Data -> 77] | [48 End Session] FAILURE (shared) Every status check's failure branch (13, 15, 17, 26, 30, 39, 41) -> 86 API Failure - Log & Render -> 87 Request Failed -> [Retry: 88 Retry Router -> the Data node that failed, chosen by last_api_alias] | [End Session: 53] ## v47 (2026-09-02) - Christina's 9/1 build guide: 2 new subflows + 3 fixes NEW BRANCH (right after Find Order succeeds, node 13): 13 -> 90 Classify - Unconfirmed Booking Check -> 91 Is Unconfirmed Booking? 91 -> [true: 93 No-PNR Bridge] | [false/default: 61, UNCHANGED normal path] SUBFLOW 1 - UNCONFIRMED BOOKING (order ref present, Edvin returns 0 PNRs, or contact reason = "Unconfirmed booking"): 90/91 detect it -> 93 builds ONE synthetic current_pnr (pnr: "", real orderReference) -> 42 GET Edvin Errands, same as the normal path from here on: 42 -> 26 -> 46 -> 1 -> 2 -> 11 -> 12 -> 25 -> 58 -> 59 -> 27 -> 3 -> 32-41 (ticket loop) -> 21 -> 22 -> 44 (errand loop, PNR sent blank/null, order reference populated) -> 30 -> 83 -> 89 -> 23. SUBFLOW 2 - ORPHAN ERRAND (no order at all): NEW button on node 77 ("No Order Reference (Log Orphan Errand)") skips Find Order (4) entirely: 77 -> 92 Orphan Entry (sets orderReference = "-999" per Elis) -> 93 (same bridge as Subflow 1, isOrphan branch) -> 42 onward, IDENTICAL to Subflow 1 from there - same channel/category/type/action selection, same free-text notes (node 12's existing per-row notes field), same ticket + errand loops. Both subflows are intentionally thin: node 93 is the only node that knows either exists. Everything from node 42 onward is the exact same code normal orders run, driven off one synthetic customer_action_pnrs entry instead of one-per-real-PNR. STILL OPEN before go-live (build guide section 6, unchanged by this session): - Confirm "Unconfirmed booking" contact reason IS Christina's "contact region" (node 90's TODO comment - strong circumstantial evidence via node 61's contact_reasons_dynamic list, not confirmed live). - Confirm Edvin's registerErrand call accepts pnr: null/"" (Subflow 1). - Confirm node 77's new button actually bypasses whatever makes Order Reference required on the existing button (verify in Zingtree admin UI - this export's formfields are empty for node 77, so that mechanism is not visible from the JSON). - Orphan-errand daily volume (Elis was checking, for prioritization only). Per Brent's commitment on the 9/1 call and Christina's guide: build as a staged/draft version, do not publish live, review with the ETG team Thursday, then run etg-errand-regression against node 27 before promoting. ## v48 (2026-09-02) - production baseline restored on top of the unified loop Brent, after comparing the v46/v47 lineage against the live production export: "production + execution log + unified loop". The v46 refactor did not delete API error handling or form validation, but it CONSOLIDATED both, and two of those consolidations lost something worth keeping. v48 keeps the unified loop and the execution log, and puts the production behaviour back on top. API ERROR HANDLING - per-request screens are back (nodes 14/16/18/28/31/40/45) Every status check still fails into 86 (log the failure, build failure_html + execution_log_html), so nothing about the log changes. 86 now continues to a NEW router, 94, which sends the agent to the screen for the request that actually failed: 86 -> 94 Failure Screen Router (last_api_alias) findorder -> 14 -> Retry -> 4 create_internal_note__no_group_id -> 16 -> Retry -> 22 create_child_ticket -> 18 -> Retry -> 33 edvin__errand_configuration -> 28 -> Retry -> 42 edvin__register_errand -> 31 -> Retry -> 43 get_side_conversation_detail -> 40 -> Retry -> 63 zingtree_redesign__update_side_conversation -> 45 -> Retry -> 66 default -> 87 -> 88 (v46 path) These are production's own screens, restored under their production node ids, which means: the screen NAMES the request, it dumps the raw response (${actions. | stringify}) for debugging, and Retry is a HARD LINK to the Data node that failed - it does not depend on last_api_alias resolving. Each screen also now prints ${transforms.execution_log_html}, so the run's read-out is on the failure screen too (that part came from v46's node 87). The generic 87 -> 88 pair is KEPT as the fallback: an alias node 94 does not know still reaches a working Retry instead of dead-ending at 53. ADDING A NEW API CALL MEANS ADDING A BUTTON TO NODE 94 *AND* NODE 88. Three of the restored screens say "${ticket_kind}" rather than "Child Ticket", because the unified loop fires 33/63/66 for grand children too. Node 85 ("Validate Grand Child Ticket") was NOT restored - node 84 covers both levels, and the per-kind counter below is the better fix for the thing node 85 was really providing (telling the agent which kind of ticket is on screen). TICKET COUNTER IS NOW PER KIND (node 32) Was: one index across every ticket in the run, so the second grand child under one child ticket read "Grand Child Ticket 3 of 4" - which says nothing about how many grand children are coming. Now each kind counts itself: Silent Ticket 1 of 1 | Child Ticket 1 of 1 | Grand Child Ticket 1 of 2 | 2 of 2 Derived from the same depth-first walk node 32 already does, so screen order still matches creation order. all_tickets_display_index / all_tickets_total keep the whole-run position for anything that wants it. FORM DATA / DYNAMIC VIEW VALIDATION - audited, one hole closed | input / view | guard | | node 77 Order Reference | 95 script -> 96 scoring -> 97 re-prompt NEW | | node 1 Type | formfield required=1 | | node 1 Notes | optional by design (prod parity) | | node 6 Agent Group | formfield required=1 | | node 6 Contact Reason FL/SC | formfield required=1 + conditional | | node 6 PNR grid (dynamic view) | 24 has_pnr_selection -> 54 -> 55 | | node 8 Passengers (dynamic view) | 9 is_selected_passengers -> 56 -> 57 | | node 12/25 customer action per PNR | 58 EVERY-row check -> 59 -> 60 | | node 47 Contact Reason (re-entry) | required=0 (prod parity, left as-is) | Node 77 was the only one with nothing enforcing it: "Order Reference*" is a MERGE FIELD, not an input, so the asterisk was decoration - a blank reference went into Find Order and came back as an API failure screen, which reads like an outage rather than a missing field. 95/96/97 follow the same script -> scoring -> re-prompt shape as the three guards that already existed. The Orphan Errand button on 77 bypasses it deliberately: no order reference is the whole point of that path. The per-PNR decision-page check (58 -> 59 -> 60) was NEVER lost in v46 - node 58 is byte-identical to production apart from a removed ZT.log, and still uses the every-row test from the 2026-08-27 fix. Verified, not assumed. DELIBERATE, DO NOT "FIX": node 29 (Clear Data) resets loop and reconciliation state but NOT the Zendesk intake values, and not `contact_reason`. Node 10 is a fresh session (Restart) and re-seeds everything from the ticket; node 29 is an Additional/Different Request CONTINUATION of the same session, and node 47's select has just written the agent's new contact reason through its score_var. Re-seeding there would throw that pick away before node 95 can write it back. STILL OPEN (not touched in v48, needs its own pass): the unresolved-selection guard. Node 27 still sets has_unresolved_selections and builds unresolved_note_html, and still nothing routes on them - a PNR whose pick cannot be resolved to a known action/bucket is silently dropped from resolved_pnrs and gets no ticket and no errand. Production has the same gap, so this is not a v46 regression. It is NOT a one-node fix: node 27 now writes only resolved_pnrs to customer_action_pnrs, so sending the agent back to node 12 would rebuild the table WITHOUT the flagged PNR - the exact trap the v24 -> v25 persisted_pnrs entry below documents. Restore persisted_pnrs in the same change or not at all. ## v51 (2026-09-04) - INTAKE MOVED TO NODE 77, AND THE TWO NO-ORDER SCREENS INTAKE IS NOW ON NODE 77 (Brent's edit, merged in here). The Agent Group radio (score_var errand_api_path) and the conditional FL/SC Contact Reason selects moved from node 6 to node 77 - the first Content node, BEFORE Edvin Find Order. Node 6's formfields are now empty; it is the PNR grid only. Why it matters beyond tidiness: the agent group and contact reason are now captured even when there is no order reference at all, which the orphan path needs, and node 90's Unconfirmed-Booking classification now sees the agent's ACTUAL contact-reason pick instead of only whatever arrived inbound (node 90 runs after node 4, which is after node 77). RESOLVER CALL SITES CHANGED (v50 had 10 / 24 / 29): the contact reason is collected on node 77, so it must be re-resolved on BOTH paths leaving it - 10 root / fresh session (clears the standardized names first) 95 Check Order Reference Provided <- the "Submit Order Reference" button 93 No-PNR Bridge <- the "No Order Reference" button 29 Clear Data <- Additional/Different Request re-entry Node 24 no longer resolves anything (node 6 collects nothing now); it just reads `contact_reason`. Four byte-identical copies of the block, same rule as before: a change to it is a change to four nodes. ORPHAN IS DERIVED, NOT FLAGGED (node 92 is gone). Node 92 "Orphan Entry" used to set errand_path_kind="orphan" and orderReference="-999"; it was deleted when the intake moved, and node 77's orphan button now points straight at node 93. Between those two changes NOTHING set the flag, so node 93 read the default "normal", took the Unconfirmed-Booking branch and would have registered against a BLANK order reference. Node 93 now derives it from the real condition - no resolved order reference - and writes errand_path_kind itself. Do not reintroduce a flag-setting node in front of it. AUTO-REGISTER vs MANUAL (Christina, 2026-09-04 call). After the internal note posts, the errand either registers itself or is handed to the agent: 15 (note OK) -> 98 Register Errand Automatically? errand_path_kind == "orphan" -> 99 build card -> 100 manual screen -> 89 default -> 44 the existing errand loop (unchanged) Christina, verbatim: "the register errand step, since there is no order to register - should it for now at least be replaced by a node saying now go to admin and register this errand", and "if they select no reference, they should see the new screen that requires manual work by them in Edvin. But if they have the reference, they should see this screen that we are seeing now." Node 99 renders ONE CARD PER ERRAND (node 27 groups on type + customer_action, so an orphan contact can still produce more than one) carrying exactly the fields she listed: Channel, Category, Type, Action, Notes, Genesys Interaction ID - plus the Zendesk ticket for traceability. Genesys interaction TYPE is deliberately NOT shown: she confirmed "it's not mandatory because it's the channel". Node 100's button carries ::zt_manual_errand_registered, so these sessions are countable in analytics. NO-PNR NOTICE (node 101, same call). The Unconfirmed Booking branch now shows the agent what happened before it drops them into type/action selection: 91 [is_unconfirmed_booking == true] -> 101 -> 93 Brent on the call: "We should have some sort of text that indicates what just happened. No PNR is available for this order." Christina: "Yes, and we need the channel." The screen names the order reference, contact reason and channel, says the airline never issued a PNR (normal for an unconfirmed booking where payment was not completed), and tells them the child ticket and internal note still happen exactly as normal. WORTH KNOWING FROM THE SAME CALL, not built: Christina said the Unconfirmed Booking contact reason is "always a fail... never schedule change" - i.e. it only ever appears under First Line, never Schedule Change. That already matches node 61's contact_reasons_dynamic lists (contact_reason__unconfirmed_booking is in fl_paths only), so nothing was changed; do not "helpfully" add it to sc_paths. OPEN, node 77: the FL contact-reason select is required=1 and the SC one is required=0. Production had both at 1. Left exactly as Brent set it rather than changed silently - decide which is intended. ## Data dictionary ### v46 (2026-09-02) - the entries that supersede everything below them - transforms.work_queue - THE structure the ticket loop walks. Built by node 27, consumed by node 32. One entry per Zendesk ticket, grand children nested inside: [ { ticket: { kind, title, pnr, bucket, category, contact_reason, customer_action, type, channel, genesys_interaction_type, errand_key, status, passengers, grand_child_tickets: [ { ...same shape... } ] }, errands: [ { ...the final_pnrs record(s) this ticket covers... } ] } ] kind is child | silent | grand_child. status is open | solved and is what node 65 sends to the Zendesk update - node 65 no longer sniffs the title for "Silent". errand_key is type + "|" + customer_action, the same key node 27/44 group on, and the join back to final_pnrs. The errands arrays hold REFERENCES to the same records final_pnrs holds, not copies - node 44 still reads final_pnrs and is unchanged. REPLACES transforms.child_tickets, which no longer exists. - Loop cursors (FORM data, no TTL): queue_index (which work_queue entry) and grandchild_index (-1 = the parent ticket itself, 0..n-1 = that grand child). Both are reset to 0 / -1 by node 27 on every pass, and clamp on entry in node 32. current_queue_index / current_is_grand_child are the position node 32 just PROCESSED - node 65 needs those, because by the time it runs the cursor has moved. is_more_tickets is node 34's routing boolean. REPLACES child_tickets_count, grandchild_tickets_count, is_more_child_tickets, is_grandchild_tickets and is_more_grandchild_tickets, all of which are gone. - transforms.resolved_ticket_ids_by_queue_index - { queue_index: zendesk_ticket_id }, written by node 65 for parent tickets only. A grand child reads its own parent's entry to fill target_ticket_id. REPLACES transforms.resolved_child_ticket_id, which only ever held "the last one resolved" and worked by luck of adjacency. - transforms.current_ticket - the ticket being processed this pass, parent or grand child. REPLACES current_child_ticket and current_grandchild_ticket. - transforms.ticket_card_html - node 84's agent card (was child_ticket_html). ticket_kind / ticket_display_index / tickets_total (FORM) drive its heading. - transforms.child_ticket - UNCHANGED NAME ON PURPOSE. CO #20's request body reads ${transforms.child_ticket.*} and lives in the admin UI, not in this export, so renaming it here would break the create call silently. It is the Zendesk payload { subject, body, orderReference, target_ticket_id }, not a ticket record. - GONE, DELIBERATELY (v46, Brent): attempted_child_ticket_keys, attempted_grandchild_ticket_keys, created_child_ticket_keys, created_grandchild_ticket_keys, registered_errand_keys, and the ticket_already_created / skip_errand_registration flags. See "THIS TREE IS AN ETL" under Conventions before reintroducing any of them. - last_api_alias (FORM data) - the Connected Object alias of the request that is about to fire, or that most recently fired. Set by one explicit ZT.setFormData("last_api_alias", "") line in the script immediately before each Data node (9, 21, 29, 32, 44, 64, 65, 93, 95); cleared only by node 10. Nodes 94 and 86 use it to name the failure, node 88 to pick the retry target. See "ENVIRONMENT FIELDS" and "SHARED FAILURE SCREEN" under Conventions. - transforms.failure_html - the failure card node 86 builds, printed by node 87. - The five Zendesk intake values - order_reference, language, contact_reason, genesys_conversation_id, genesys_interaction_type - see "ENVIRONMENT FIELDS" under Conventions for where each one is read and written. - transforms.channel / transforms.category: full Edvin errand-config OBJECTS {id,name,categories}. Set in node 46. Store only .name on PNR items (see node 2). - transforms.customer_action_pnrs: array of PNR items {pnr, channel(name), channelId, category(name), categoryId, type, typeId, notes, actions_array}. Built in node 2, restitched in node 27. - actions_array item: {id, name, bucket(STRING), actionId, ...}. bucket normalized to a string in node 2 (bucketKey). - transforms.child_tickets: [{child_ticket:{...grandchild_tickets:[]}}]. Built node 27 by grouping stitched PNRs on the DISTINCT (type+action) key: proceed -> ONE active child (grandchildren = one per distinct type+action, only when 2+ combos); non-proceed -> ONE silent ticket per distinct (type+action). Consumed node 32 loop. - transforms.child_ticket_html (v41, undocumented until now): the agent-facing card rendered by node 84 (Content, `${transforms.child_ticket_html}`). Built in node 32 by buildErrandCardHtml(), which reads .title/.pnr/.bucket/.customer_action/.type/ .formatted_passengers/.passengers off its payload argument - that shape belongs to transforms.current_child_ticket (= child_tickets[cursor].child_ticket, set earlier in node 32), NOT the local `child_ticket` object node 32 also builds a few lines later for node 33's Zendesk create call (subject/body/orderReference/target_ticket_id only - no pnr/passengers). Passing the wrong one is exactly what produced a blank "PNR " title and "No passenger details available" on every card - see changelog. - transforms.final_pnrs: one entry per distinct (type+action). Built node 27 (deduped), consumed ONLY by node 44 (registers one Edvin errand each). v19: node 21 no longer reads it - the internal note reads transforms.customer_action_pnrs so every PNR appears, even when two PNRs share the same type AND action (ZD 7621694). FIXED 2026-08-21 (ZD 337619): each final_pnrs entry used to spread group[0] alone, so an errand covering 2+ PNRs silently dropped every PNR after the first from the Edvin message. buildFinalErrandRecord() (node 27) now combines the whole group - pnr becomes the joined PNR list (joinPnrs), passengers/formatted_passengers are unioned and de-duped, orderReference is the de-duped set joined - before node 44 formats it. FIXED 2026-08-21's pass missed .notes - it stayed on the group[0] spread, so a second PNR's agent notes were dropped from the Edvin "Agent Notes" line whenever 2+ PNRs collapsed into one errand. FIXED 2026-08-24: mergeNotes(group) now builds notes as "PNR: note | PNR: note" (non-empty, de-duped) before node 44 formats it. See changelog. - transforms.unresolved_selections: [{pnr, field, raw, reason, reason_text, bucket, type}] - every PNR whose selection could not be turned into (action + known bucket). Built node 27, rendered by node 27 into transforms.unresolved_note_html for node 51, counted by node 21's log. - has_unresolved_selections / unresolved_selections_count (FORM data): node 50's routing boolean and its count. Form data because logic-node expressions read scalars by name. - transforms.attempted_child_ticket_keys / attempted_grandchild_ticket_keys (v35): the titles this session has ATTEMPTED to create. Recorded by nodes 32 and 36 BEFORE the create fires; read by those same nodes as the duplicate guard that nodes 13/15 route on. These - not the created_* lists - are what stop a duplicate ticket. - transforms.created_child_ticket_keys / created_grandchild_ticket_keys: titles Zendesk CONFIRMED (nodes 14/16, 2xx only). RECONCILIATION INPUT ONLY since v35 - node 21 compares them against planned_ticket_titles to warn about a ticket it cannot prove exists. Do not route a duplicate guard off these again; see Conventions. - transforms.registered_errand_keys (v35): one entry per (type|customer_action) already sent to Edvin this session. Recorded by node 44 before node 43 fires; node 17 routes on it. Deliberately NOT cleared by node 27, so a Back-nav replay cannot re-register an errand Edvin already holds, while a selection the agent genuinely changed makes a new key and registers normally. - skip_errand_registration (FORM data, v35): node 17's routing boolean. True when this errand's key is already registered, or when the cursor has no item at all. - transforms.planned_ticket_titles: every child/silent/grandchild title this run intends to create. Built node 27, compared in node 21 against created_child_ticket_keys + created_grandchild_ticket_keys so the note cannot promise a ticket Zendesk never confirmed. - grandchild_parent_resolved / grandchild_parent_blocked (FORM data, v36, restructured v37): routing booleans set by whichever check node in the resolve chain last ran (18, 28, or 55) and tested by that attempt's router (19, 30, or 56). resolved=true means targetTicketId was proven this pass (grandchild_parent_id now holds it); blocked=true is set ONLY by node 55, the final attempt, when resolution never happened across all 3 tries. Mutually exclusive by construction; reset per child ticket by node 39, and by nodes 10/29 between sessions. v37 DROPPED child_ticket_resolve_attempts (v36's poll counter) - which attempt is running is now which node you are at (18=1st, 28=2nd, 55=3rd/final), not runtime state. See Conventions "GRANDCHILD-PARENT RESOLVE CHAIN" for why. - transforms.blocked_grandchild_parent_keys / blocked_grandchild_ticket_titles (v36): written by node 55 (the final resolve-chain attempt) only when all 3 tries came up empty. The first is the child ticket's title (for diagnostics); the second is every grandchild title under it that was NEVER attempted (not pushed to attempted_grandchild_ticket_keys, since node 36 never ran for them). Node 21 prints these as a distinct BLOCKED line, and excludes them from the generic "not confirmed" reconciliation warning so the two states are never conflated. Reset by nodes 10/29. - Counters: child_tickets_count, grandchild_tickets_count (form data, no TTL) and transforms.final_pnrs_count (node 44). All three clamp on entry and reset to 0 when exhausted, so every loop is re-runnable - final_pnrs_count only since v35. - Display counters (FORM data, v43): child_ticket_display_index/child_tickets_total (node 32, read by node 84's "Create Child Ticket X of Y" heading), grandchild_ticket_display_index/grandchild_tickets_total (node 36, node 85's heading), errand_display_index/final_pnrs_total (node 44, node 78's heading). Each is the 1-based position of the item about to be processed THIS pass (cursor value + 1, read before that cursor increments), paired with the loop's total length. Purely presentational - never read by logic nodes or Connected Objects; do not confuse with the *_count cursor variables above, which are 0-based and drive the loop itself. - has_customer_action_selection (FORM data, v43, fixed 2026-08-27): node 58's routing boolean, gating new Scoring node 59 between node 25 and node 27. True only when EVERY row in transforms.customer_action_pnrs has a non-blank customer_action__ (originally .some() - any ONE row - which is the bug the 2026-08-27 correction entry fixed). transforms.missing_customer_action_pnrs (node 58) lists the PNRs still blank, rendered on node 60. Distinct from has_unresolved_selections (node 27, existing) - see the v43 section below. - Counters (form data, no TTL): child_tickets_count, grandchild_tickets_count; booleans is_more_child_tickets, is_grandchild_tickets, is_more_grandchild_tickets, is_more_pnrs, isMorePNR. - actions.edvin__errand_configuration, actions.get_edvin_prop_long_value: Edvin API responses. ## External systems (CX Actions / Connected Objects) Edvin: Find Order (4), GET Edvin Errands (42), Register Errand (43). Zendesk: Update Tags (31), Create Child Ticket (33), Create Grandchild Ticket (37), Get Side Conversations (40), Add Internal Note (22). ## Conventions & gotchas - ENVIRONMENT FIELDS - THREE PLACES, ONE ID EACH. This tree runs against ONE Zendesk org at a time. Five values arrive as inbound query parameters named after that org's ticket-field ids, and the tree standardises them immediately: Zendesk field this export (dev, org 116) tree name Order_Reference custom_field_33772689958162 order_reference Language custom_field_28137345621650 language Contact_Reason custom_field_29559177650834 contact_reason Genesys_Conversation_ID custom_field_31975964556050 genesys_conversation_id Genesys_Interaction_Type custom_field_31213052370194 genesys_interaction_type READ once, in node 10 (root). WRITE BACK in node 95, and only for the two the agent can change on node 77 - order_reference and contact_reason - and only when the value is non-empty, so a blank never clears a field the ticket already holds. DECLARE in predefined_vars. Nothing else in the tree may name a custom_field_ id: every other node reads the tree name. A promote or demote therefore touches exactly those three places, and the `etg-env-promote` skill's remapper is what does it. Do NOT reintroduce the dual-id table that read the prod id with the dev id as a fallback and then fanned the resolved value back out to both: it makes a stray reference to the WRONG org's field resolve to a real value instead of an empty one, which is how a cross-environment value becomes a stale reference nobody can see. orderReference (camelCase) is a deliberate mirror of order_reference, kept only because at least one Connected Object request body in the admin UI reads that name. Retire it once every CO body is confirmed to read order_reference. Node 93 sets order_reference to the orphan sentinel "-999" for Edvin. That is session state and is deliberately NOT written back to the Zendesk field. - NO EXECUTION LOG, NO SHARED BLOCKS. The tree had an `execution_log` form variable with logArm/logFlush/logWrite pasted byte-identically into 12 scripts and a node 89 that rendered it. All of it is gone. What survives is the one thing that actually routed: `last_api_alias`, now written by a single explicit ZT.setFormData line in the script before each Data node. Nothing else in this tree may reintroduce a helper block copied into two nodes - if two nodes need the same code, the design is wrong. WHAT WENT WITH IT, if it is ever wanted back: the per-step OK/FAIL read-out that nodes 23, 48, 53 and the failure screens printed, and node 89's end-of-run "actual vs planned" receipt (tickets created and errands registered against what node 27 planned). Rebuild the receipt from tree state - work_queue, resolved_ticket_ids_by_queue_index, final_pnrs - not from a log. - UNIFIED TICKET LOOP (v46). Child, silent and grand child tickets all run through ONE loop body: 32 -> 84 -> 33 -> 17 -> 62 -> 64 -> 63 -> 39 -> 65 -> 66 -> 41 -> 34. The old grandchild body (36, 37, 38, 68, 69, 70, 71, 72, 85 and status checks 19, 20, 49, 50, 51, 52, plus router 35) called the SAME three Connected Objects as the child body - #20 create, #158 get details, #207 update - so it was a verbatim clone whose only real difference was target_ticket_id. It is deleted. Node 32 walks work_queue depth-first: the parent ticket, then each of its grand children, then the next entry. That ORDER IS THE CONTRACT - a parent is always created and resolved before its grand children, which is the only reason a grand child can read its parent's id out of resolved_ticket_ids_by_queue_index. Do not reorder the walk without moving that lookup. PLATFORM RISK TO WATCH IN SANDBOX: node 32 is now re-entered once per TICKET rather than once per child ticket, so a run with a child plus three grand children hits it four times instead of one. Zingtree's engine flags repeated re-entry into the same node or short node cycle as an "invalid loop" independently of whether the counter logic is correct (Brent hit exactly this on v36 - see the v37 resolve-chain entry). The loop passes through Content node 84 every pass, which is the paced-checkpoint shape that fixed it last time, but this is the one thing in v45 the offline harness cannot see. Test it live before promoting. - THIS TREE IS AN ETL, AND API ERROR HANDLING IS THE SAFEGUARD (v46, Brent's call, 2026-09-02). Load the order from Edvin, let the agent pick PNRs / passengers / type / customer actions, build one data structure from those picks, then fire the sequence programmatically: create ticket -> get details -> update -> grand children if any -> next ticket -> internal note -> register errands -> close. There is NO "have I already created this?" check anywhere, by design. History, so nobody re-derives it: v44 and everything before it CARRIED such guards - attempted_child_ticket_keys, created_*_keys, registered_errand_keys, and the ticket_already_created / skip_errand_registration flags - but no node ever routed on them. They had been dead code since the v42 renumbering broke the node ids the older claude.md entries name ("node 13/15", "node 45"). v45 wired them up as nodes 90/91; Brent removed both the same day. The guards were state that pretended to be a safety net, and a replay they suppressed silently was worse to debug than one that shows up in the log. What actually protects a run now: every API call is status-checked, every failure routes to the shared failure screen (86 -> 94 -> per-request screen, or 87/88). A Back-nav replay of node 27 DOES re-run the ETL and DOES create a second set of tickets. That is accepted rather than suppressed: a replay that shows up in Zendesk is easier to debug than one a key list silently swallowed. If duplicates ever become a real operational problem, the fix is upstream - stop node 25's Back from re-entering node 27 - not a key list inside the loop. - SHARED FAILURE SCREEN. Every status check's failure branch goes to 86 (script: grade the call from actions[last_api_alias]._zt_meta, build failure_html) -> 94 (screen router) -> the per-request screen for that alias, or 87 -> 88 (retry router) as the fallback. Both routers branch on last_api_alias. ADDING A NEW API CALL MEANS ADDING A BUTTON TO NODE 94 *AND* NODE 88, AND A ZT.setFormData("last_api_alias", "") LINE TO THE SCRIPT BEFORE ITS DATA NODE. If you forget, its Retry falls through node 88's default straight to node 53 (Session Ended) - the run ends safely, but the agent cannot retry. - A DUPLICATE GUARD MUST RECORD THE ATTEMPT, NOT THE CONFIRMATION (v35, learned from ZD 334818). v25 made nodes 14/16 record a title only on a confirmed 2xx, so that a failed create would still be retried and flagged. But the guards read those same lists - so a create Zendesk actually MADE and reported badly stayed unrecorded, and the next pass created a second ticket. The two jobs need two lists: attempted_* for the guard (written before the call), created_* for the note's warning (written after). When in doubt, prefer a note that says "not confirmed - check the ticket list" over a duplicate written against a customer's order. - EVERY CURSOR LOOP CLAMPS ON ENTRY AND RESETS ON EXHAUSTION. Node 44 was the one loop missing both, so after a full pass its cursor sat at final_pnrs.length and a replay read final_pnrs[out-of-range] === undefined - registering a REAL Edvin errand with no type, action or PNR. Nodes 32 and 36 are the reference shape. - This tree is RE-ENTERED ROUTINELY. Node 25 has Back enabled and keep_vars_on_back=1, so Back + Continue re-fires node 27 and everything downstream of it. Any node that writes to Zendesk or Edvin must be idempotent under that replay - test it, don't assume it. walk.mjs (Workflow JSONs/ETG/) walks the real continuation graph and counts the actual create calls; the offline harness stubs them and cannot see this class of bug. - Transforms expire after 1 hour; node 29 Clear Data resets loop state so the outer "Additional request" loop restarts clean. - Node 3 guard (len(transforms.child_tickets) >= 1) MUST stay before node 32 — node 32->33 creates a Zendesk ticket unconditionally, so an empty set has to skip to 21. - BUCKET LABELS vs ROUTING KEYS (v31/v32 - the cause of "bucket is not one Zingtree routes on"). Edvin returns the bucket as an OBJECT {id, name} where `name` is a HUMAN LABEL, not the snake_case key this tree branches on. bucketKey() only extracted that label, so node 27 - which trims and lowercases before testing KNOWN_BUCKETS - accepted "Proceed" (it happens to lowercase into the key) and rejected everything else. VERIFIED against the live errand-configuration response (2026-08-04). Across all three channels and all thirteen categories Edvin uses exactly THREE buckets, ids stable: id 3 "No action" -> no_action id 4 "Proceed" -> proceed id 5 "Different request" -> different_request There is NO "escalate" bucket in Edvin. KNOWN_BUCKETS still lists it; that is harmless (it never occurs) - do not invent a mapping for it. Measured on the real Cancellation category (17 types, 137 action slots): the pre-fix build rejected 88 of 137 - every No action and every Different request. v32 routes all 137, split proceed 49 / no_action 75 / different_request 13. v32 MATCHES ON THE BUCKET ID FIRST (BUCKET_BY_ID). The id is the contract; the label is display text ETG can reword at any time, and a reworded label silently breaks a name-only map. BUCKET_BY_NAME is the fallback for a bucket that arrives as a bare string. An unmapped bucket is returned UNCHANGED, never guessed - node 27 then flags it and stops the run, because guessing no_action for something that might mean Proceed records "the customer declined" against a customer who did not. Node 46 logs "edvin bucket labels seen: [...]" every session. KEEP THE BLOCK IDENTICAL IN NODES 2 AND 46 - both feed node 27; drift means the same action routes two different ways. Verified by realsweep.mjs against edvin_real.json. - bucket routing keys: proceed | no_action | escalate | different_request. As of v24 an unrecognized or blank bucket is NO LONGER a default-to-silent-ticket; it is a problem that halts the run at node 50. - UNUSABLE SELECTIONS NEVER GET RECORDED (v24, the rule that matters most here): a PNR that does not resolve to a real action with a known bucket must not become a ticket or an Edvin errand. "We could not read the selection" and "the customer declined" produce identical output otherwise, and only one of them is safe to write against an order. Node 27 classifies the problem (selection_unreadable | lookup_failed | bucket_missing | bucket_unrecognized), writes EMPTY child_tickets/final_pnrs, and sets has_unresolved_selections; node 50 routes to node 51, which sends the agent back to node 12 to re-pick. Do not "fix" this by restoring the old warning-in-the-note behaviour - the note used to apologize for a fact it had already recorded. - NO
